title: Writing: A Scientific Summary and Critical Evaluation

writingModel.placeholder: Introduce the study: what was investigated and why it matters
writingModel.hint: State the topic, the gap in knowledge, and why it was investigated

writingModel.placeholder: Describe the methodology — sample, procedure, controls
writingModel.hint: Use passive and hedging: "approximately X participants were selected…"
Use: "Results suggest…", "Approximately…", "The group that X performed considerably better than…"
Comparatives: "The study was considerably more rigorous than…" / "The sample was smaller than…"

writingModel.placeholder: Conclude with implications and need for further research
writingModel.hint: "These findings may have implications for… / Further research is needed to establish whether…"

writingTemplate.suffix: , a question of considerable scientific significance.
writingTemplate.placeholder: the relationship between open data practices and replication rates
writingTemplate.hint: Introduce the research question — use noun phrase

writingTemplate.suffix: participants were recruited and randomly assigned to ___.
writingTemplate.hint: Describe the sample and design with hedging
Report findings with hedging verb + comparative for effect size
writingTemplate.placeholder: open data practices are associated with higher replication rates / considerably smaller than anticipated

writingTemplate.hint: Use "while" for contrast; comparative for evaluation
writingTemplate.placeholder: considerably more rigorous than previous studies / its relatively small and non-representative sample

writingTemplate.prefix: Further research is needed to establish whether
writingTemplate.hint: Hedge the conclusion — "needed to establish whether + clause"
writingTemplate.placeholder: these findings generalise to other scientific disciplines / the precise mechanisms underlying the observed effects

items: This study aimed to investigate the relationship between X and Y.
There is currently considerable debate about whether X causes Y.
Previous research has suggested that X may be associated with Y.
It remains unclear whether X is a causal factor or merely a correlate.
This study addressed a significant gap in the existing literature.
The results suggest that X is associated with Y.
Participants in the experimental group tended to perform considerably better.
Approximately 60% of the sample showed measurable improvement.
The effect size, while statistically significant, was smaller than anticipated.
These findings appear to be consistent with previous research on this topic.
The methodology was considerably more rigorous than that of earlier studies.
The sample size was larger than average for this type of research.
Effect sizes were not as large as those reported in initial pilot studies.
The more carefully variables were controlled, the more consistent the results became.
The control group showed significantly fewer improvements than the experimental group.
These findings may have important implications for X.
Further research is needed to establish whether these results are replicable.
It is likely that the effect will be smaller in a more diverse population.
There is some evidence that X may contribute to Y, though causation cannot yet be confirmed.
These results are best interpreted as preliminary and should be replicated before conclusions are drawn.

questions.text: "The experimental group performed ___ better than the control group across all measures." (considerably)
"___ 150 participants were recruited from the general population." (imprecise quantity)
"The results ___ that open data is associated with higher replication rates." (medium-strength hedge)
"The ___ carefully variables were controlled, the ___ consistent the findings became." (proportional)
"It remains ___ whether the effects will replicate in a more diverse population." (impersonal hedge)
questions.hint: "It remains unclear whether + clause" = formal impersonal hedge

questions.text: "This study proves that open science improves research quality" is an appropriately hedged scientific claim.
questions.hint: "Proves" is too strong — use "suggests," "indicates," or "appears to"

questions.text: "These findings ___ have important implications for how journals evaluate submissions." (possibility)
"Effect sizes were not ___ large as those reported in initial pilot studies." (below equal)
questions.hint: "Not as + adjective + as" = lower than the comparison point
